title: UFC Fight Night prediction -- Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira: Card, odds, start time, where to watch
text: UFC Fight Night prediction -- Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira: Card, odds, start time, where to watch One of the heavyweight division's most enduring veterans fights an intriguing new addition Derrick Lewis will cash a check against anyone. Tallison Teixeira seeks to expedite his rise by beating a heavyweight stalwart. Their clashing philosophies meet at UFC Fight Night in Nashville on Saturday. Lewis (28-12, 1 NC) has carved his niche in mixed martial arts. "The Black Beast" is the record holder for most UFC knockouts and has fought twice for UFC gold. Most fighters are obsessed with being a champion, but Lewis' outlook is refreshingly grounded. Lewis, 40, does not care who stands across from him so long as he's getting paid. MMA is prize fighting after all. "It's always been the number one thing, even when I started," Lewis told CBS Sports. "I was fighting every other month before I was in the UFC. That's how I'd pay my rent. My rent was $525 a month. I'd fight every other month, $500 to show and $500 to win. That's how we'd make ends meet. "I never care who's next. So long as I get to fight, it's all I care about." Check out the full interview with Derrick Lewis below. Teixeira (8-0) is the latest rookie testing himself against the KO artist. Teixeira enters UFC Fight Night as the betting favorite despite having five times less experience than Lewis. What little we've seen from the towering heavyweight, whose reach exceeds Alexander Volkov's, is impressive. Teixeira has racked up eight consecutive first-round KOs, recently stopping Justin Tafa in 35 seconds. He's already ranked No. 13 in the shallow heavyweight division. Beating 11-year veteran Lewis likely ranks him in the top 10 after only two Octagon appearances. "Training for Derrick was different than ever before. It was very intense," Teixeira told CBS Sports through a Portuguese interpreter. "He's a tough opponent. When heavyweights connect with four-ounce gloves, you go out. He's very dangerous. "Look at how tall and strong I am. I think I can be a bigger problem for him than everyone has ever been." Saturday's main event won't jump off the page but should produce a great KO. Fortunately, it's supported by intriguing main card fights. Stephen "Wonderboy" Thompson fends off Gabriel Bonfim. Steve Garcia and Calvin Kattar promises great MMA boxing. Beloved brawler Nate Landwehr is also on the card. Below is the rest of the fight card for Saturday with the latest odds before we predict the main event. If "The Black Beast" gets in close, he'll have ample room to fire big shots through his opponent's guard. It's tough assessing a young fighter who has never gone past the first round. How will fatigue affect Teixeira late? Will his power carry late? Are his skills refined enough to execute backup plans? title: Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira prediction, pick: Who gets KO'd at UFC Nashville?
text: Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira prediction, pick: Who gets KO'd at UFC Nashville? Heavyweights headline UFC's return to 'Music City' MMA Junkie analyst Dan Tom goes in-depth to break down the biggest fights in the UFC. Today, he takes a closer look at the UFC on ESPN 70 main event between Derrick Lewis and Tallison Teixeira. Derrick Lewis UFC on ESPN 70 preview Staple info: - Record: 28-12 MMA, 19-10 UFC - Height: 6'3" Age: 40 Weight: 261 lbs. Reach: 79" - Last fight: TKO win over Rodrigo Nascimento (May 11, 2024) - Camp: Main Street Boxing and Muay Thai (Texas) - Stance/striking style: Orthodox/kickboxing - Risk management: Fair Supplemental info: - + Legacy FC heavyweight title - + Regional MMA accolades - + 23 KO victories - + 1 submission win - + 9 first-round finishes - + KO power - + Dangerous overhands and uppercuts - + Underrated kicks and knees - + Strong inside the clinch - ^ Strikes well off the breaks - + Shows improved wrestling - + Deceptive scrambling/getup ability - + Devastating ground striker Tallison Teixeira UFC on ESPN 70 preview Staple info: - Record: 8-0 MMA, 1-0 UFC - Height: 6'7" Age: 25 Weight: 259 lbs. Reach: 83" - Last fight: TKO win over Justin Tafa (Feb. 8, 2025) - Camp: Team Lucas Mineiro (Brazil) - Stance/striking style: Orthodox/kickboxing - Risk management: Fair Supplemental info: - + Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt - + Multiple grappling accolades - + Muay Thai red kruang - + 7 KO victories - + 1 submission win - + 8 first-round finishes - + KO power - + Dangerous right hand - + Dynamic kicks - ^ Variates looks and levels - + Servicable takedown game - ^ Favors doubles along the fence - + Competent submission skills Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira point of interest: Heavyweight hands The main event in Nashville features a heavyweight showdown between Derrick Lewis and Tallison Teixeira. Stepping onto the scene as an unabashed brawler, Lewis has shown some signs of improvement underneath the scary destructions that often take place in his fights. An athletic mover for his size, Lewis can throw accurate knees and head kicks with little signs of struggle. A downright scary distance closer when he chooses to be, Lewis can force his opponents into the fence whether or not he lands on them, almost in a juggernaut-like fashion. With a frame that is hard to control in close, the 40-year-old slugger does his best work when striking off the breaks, maintaining a dangerous potency in small spaces that go deep into the fight. Lewis also has an appetite for the counter, showing that he’s not beyond setting traps and playing possum in order to draw his opponents into his uncanny power. That said, Lewis will still need to respect what is coming his way this Saturday. Enter Teixiera. Although Teixiera is clearly lacking in the experience department, I can see why many are high on the prospects of this young heavyweight. Despite Teixeira's insane height, he actually moves quite well for a big man and is not afraid to utilize tools like a long jab. The Brazilian also packs wicked power in his rear hand, but kicks, particularly to the body, may serve Teixeira well in this spot. Teixeira may not go to the body as much as I'd like, but he has shown some decent change-ups from front teeps to Thai kicks that help exentuate his length. Teixeira will blitz forward in combination when he's feeling in stride, but he'll need to be careful about crowding his work into the clinch – an area where Lewis can stage comebacks. Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira breakdown: Potential grappling threats Considering the high potential for chaos on the feet, no one should be shocked if this party hits the floor. Despite Lewis showing improved offensive wrestling and a surprising ability to hit inside trips in recent years, Teixeira is the more dangerous grappler on paper. Although we've seen very little of Teixeira's ground game, the 25-year-old owns a Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt and has apparently been grappling since childhood. Teixeira only has one submission win on his resume, but between that win being an inverted triangle-armbar to his history training with Antonio Rodrigo Nogueira, I suspect that the lengthy heavyweight has solid dexterity to boot. When it comes to wrestling, Teixeira has shown a servicable double leg he can go to when his opponents find their back against the fence. That said, effectively taking down and grounding someone like Lewis is easier said than done. Traditionally dealing with fighters who are trying to grapple him, Lewis wields deceptively effective counter-grappling tactics. Whether he’s hoisting his opponent up with a whizzer or shucking someone off with an underhook, Lewis has been hard to take down along the fence, as single legs or outside trips in open space seem to be what gets him grounded most. Even when successfully taken down, Lewis still offers a lot of sneaky static in regard to stymying submission attempts and strikes. Like a sand shark lying in wait, Lewis plays a conservative game when put on his back, keeping his arms in tight for safety while waiting for the right moment to explode (usually timing his opposition when they’re in transition). Once allowed the smallest of space for momentum, Lewis will force his way to his base, turtling to a tripod position to stand. As someone who is a fan of this style of get-up, I can tell you that it can be a nightmare to encounter when executed properly. For example, Lewis – while keeping his base firmly beneath him – will maintain an angle on his back that resembles a steep ski slope. Although this tripod position invites back-takes to the naked eye, the downward slope Lewis keeps serves as a trap, making eager back takers ultimately slide forward and lose position (all while allowing the Texas native to stand back up). And if Lewis is able to end up on top via swimming for underhooks and shucking, then we could see a drastic shift in this matchup’s momentum given the hellfire of ground-and-pound he provides. Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira odds The oddsmakers and the public are favoring the undefeated fighter, listing Teixeira -245 and Lewis +186 via FanDuel. Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira prediction, pick Considering how high the MMA gambling world gets over youthful, undefeated products, I can't say that I'm surprised to see Teixeira installed as the betting favorite despite being relatively unproven. Should Teixeira come out and light Lewis up with some body kicks, then no one should be shocked if the Brazilian can find a finish soon after. That said, Lewis has had a penchant for both countering and coming back from effective body kicks – particularly against taller opponents. In fact, whenever facing fighters of a similar height to Teixeira, Lewis has traditionally done fairly well (going 3-0 in the UFC opposite the likes of Travis Browne, Alexander Volkov and Jack May). And if Teixeira decides to revert to his base of grappling, then he could find himself in a frying pan-to-frier situation. Despite logic saying that Lewis should be beatable on the ground, only a select few fighters (Daniel Cormier, Serghei Spivac and Jailton Almeida) have been able to truly out-grapple the American, as anyone who tries to grapple Lewis has traditionally done poorly. Should Teixeira fall into this classic trap, then he'll need to be careful not to end up underneath Lewis, which is almost a death sentence given his lethal ground striking. I ultimately suspect that it's a strike off the break that sparks things off for Lewis, likely after having to survive some scares first. The pick is Lewis by knockout in Round 2. Prediction: Lewis inside the distance Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira start time, how to watch As the main event, Lewis and Teixeira are expected to make their walks to the octagon at approximately 11:45 p.m. ET. The fight airs on ESPN and streams on ESPN+.

title: UFC Nashville fight card picks & predictions for Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira
text: UFC Nashville fight card picks & predictions for Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira The UFC returns this weekend with a UFC Fight Night card in Nashville, TN, and MMA KO’s Drew Beaupré is here to provide predictions for all 12 fights on the card. The event is headlined by top-ranked heavyweights Derrick Lewis and Tallison Teixeira, who debuted in the UFC with a 35-second knockout earlier this year and now gets a huge step up in competition against the promotion’s all-time leader in knockouts. The night’s co-main event is a welterweight bout featuring former title challenger Stephen “Wonderboy” Thompson and Gabriel Bonfim. Thompson comes into the night looking to snap a two-fight skid and collect his first win since 2022, while Bonfim has won two fights in a row after being upset by Nicolas Dalby in 2023. UFC Nashville Main Card Predictions Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira This may finally be the fight where Lewis comes up short against a rising heavyweight prospect, but until I see that happen I have to pick “The Black Beast” to score another finish and add to his legacy as the UFC’s all-time knockout leader. (Pick: Lewis) READ MORE: UFC star Conor McGregor eyes return at White House card despite Dana White's doubt Stephen Thompson vs. Gabriel Bonfim Thompson has obviously slowed down considerably at this stage of his career, but given that Bonfim’s best path to victory is on the ground I’m going to slightly lean with “Wonderboy” to stifle the Brazilian’s takedown attempts and pull off an upset in Nashville. (Pick: Thompson) Calvin Kattar vs. Steve Garcia While Garcia’s current streak of knockouts is certainly impressive, Kattar’s own striking skills and the fact that he’s never been knocked out should allow him to spoil his opponent’s momentum and also snap his current four-fight skid. (Pick: Kattar) Nate Landwehr vs. Morgan Charriere This is one of the best matchups at UFC Nashville as well as a potential Fight of the Night contender. Charriere is certainly the more technical fighter, but I think that Landwehr can survive any big shots and outwork “The Last Pirate” to get back into the win column. (Pick: Landwehr) Vitor Petrino vs. Austen Lane I don’t know how far Petrino will be able to go in the UFC heavyweight division in the long run, but he does have the knockout power necessary to stop Lane and kick off his time in a new weight class with a big victory. (Pick: Petrino) Junior Tafa vs. Tuco Tokkos Tafa is in the opposite position of Petrino as a former heavyweight dropping down to 205 lbs., but as long as his power translates to a new division then he should be able to handle Tokkos in what could be the 35-year-old’s final fight in the UFC. (Pick: Tafa) READ MORE: Merab Dvalishvili teases next fight plans after meeting with UFC brass UFC Nashville Preliminary Card Predictions Chris Curtis vs. Max Griffin There was a point in Griffin’s career where I think he’d be able to stifle Curtis’ striking and pull of the upset here, but at this stage I think “The Action Man” will just be too much too much for him to handle. (Pick: Curtis) Jake Matthews vs. Chidi Njokuani Njokuani is currently on the best run of his UFC career after snapping a three-fight losing streak. Matthews will certainly be a tough test, but if the American can keep things standing then he should be able to get the job done here. (Pick: Njokuani) Lauren Murphy vs. Eduarda Moura Murphy is the kind of experienced veteran that could have bested the younger Moura at one point in her career, but this is a tough matchup for her to come back to after two and a half years out of the cage. (Pick: Moura) Kennedy Nzechukwu vs. Valter Walker Despite the fact that Nzechukwu is a more than 2-1 favorite, this feels like one of the tougher fights to call at UFC Nashville. Walker has never been knocked out, but even if he can’t stop him with strikes I still think Nzechukwu is well-rounded enough to earn his third-straight win. (Pick: Nzechukwu) READ MORE: UFC CEO Dana White claims Fourth of July White House event will be 'exceptional' Mike Davis vs. Mitch Ramirez Davis’ four-fight win streak came to an end in his last outing against Fares Ziam, but this matchup with Ramirez is a good spot for “Beast Boy” to get back on track ahead of what will hopefully be a more active schedule going forward. (Pick: Davis) Fatima Kline vs. Melissa Martinez Kline’s debut loss in a short-notice flyweight bout with Jasmine Jasudavicius has aged well given that Jasudavicius is now the promotion’s #5-ranked flyweight contender, and “The Archangel” should move closer towards the strawweight rankings with a win over Melissa Martinez in Nashville. (Pick: Kline) MMA KO will be providing comprehensive coverage for UFC Nashville all throughout fight week, and be sure to check back on our homepage tomorrow for live results and highlights on fight night. title: UFC Nashville odds: Best betting props, parlays and picks | Lewis vs. Teixeira
text: UFC Nashville goes down this weekend (Sat., July 12, 2025) inside Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tennessee. The main event features Heavyweights with Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira. Lewis, a divisional stalwart, is hoping to get past the UFC neophyte and secure a fight with new UFC champion, Tom Aspinall. When it comes to the rest of the UFC Nashville card, there’s not too much to write home about. The co-main is Stephen Thompson vs. Gabriel Bonfim. Rounding out the main card is Calvin Kattar vs. Steve Garcia, Nate Landwehr vs. Morgan Charriere, Vitor Petrino vs. Austin Lane and Junior Tafa vs Tuco Tokkos. UFC Nashville’s “Prelims” are headlined by Max Griffin vs. Chris Curtis. The “Prelims” also have Jake Matthews vs. Chidi Njokuani and Lauren Murphy vs. Eduarda Moura. As always, there’s lots to bet on this card and we’ve got odds for all the fights below: UFC Nashville Main Card Money Line Odds Derrick Lewis (+220) vs. Tallison Teixeira (-270) The towering Teixeira is just 8-0 and two fights into his UFC career. He debuted in the Octagon with a Contender Series first round knockout over Arthur Lopes. In his proper debut, he put away Justin Tafa in 35 seconds (see it here). Lewis — who turned 40 this year — is coming off a third round technical knockout win over Rodrigo Nascimento. Before that, he lost a five-round decision to Jailton Almeida. And before that, he scored a 33-second win over Marcos Rogerio Lima (see it here). That win snapped a three fight losing skid (all finishes) where he lost to Serghei Spivac, Sergei Pavlovich and Tai Tuivasa. There’s not much to scout when it comes to Teixeira. He’s very tall and very long and he’s coming into UFC in his athletic prime at only 25 years-old. Lewis is giving up four inches of height and four inches of reach to the young Brazilian. The last time Lewis fought someone with that kind of reach it was Pavlovich and he lasted just 55 seconds. Lewis is capable of the spectacular and shocking in an Octagon. But, it really feels like the odds are stacked against him here, with a fighter so long, so powerful and with so much youth on his side. Lewis’ defense against significant strikes is just 40 percent. That spells a lot of trouble for “The Black Beast” against a man who, so far, has landed 14.61 significant strikes per-minute across his three Octagon appearances. In Heavyweight, it only takes one punch to win, a lot of the times, but I have to favor the man who is going to be landing dozens of them in a round (if it makes it that far). The round total for this fight is set at 1.5. I think the under is most likely, as do many others. The odds are just -210 for that prop. Teixeira by KO/TKO/DQ is a laughable -185. And Teixeira to win by strikes in round one is just -125. Clearly, there’s not much value if you believe Teixeira is going to quickly separate Lewis from his consciousness (as I do). For my best bet, I’m going to go for a winning round and method of victory parlay. I’m taking round one and TKO/KO/DQ. This covers me just in case Lewis does something silly/outstanding in the first round in Nashville. Best bet: Fight to end in Round 1 by KO/TKO/DQ (-150) Stephen Thompson (+320) vs. Gabriel Bonfim (-410) Thompson is coming off a third round knockout loss to Joaquin Buckley (see it here). Before that, he was submitted by Shavkat Rakhmonov (see it here). His last win was over Kevin Holland, when Holland retired at the end of round four. Bonfim, on the other hand, choked out Khaos Williams in his last fight (see it here). Before that, he took a decision over Ange Loosa. Before those fights he lost, as a big favorite, to Nicolas Dalby via technical knockout (see it here). I don’t think Thompson is long for this sport. He turned 42 this year and his fighting style isn’t great for masking your age. He can’t hide behind takedowns and take dangerous finishers out of their comfort zones. He has to stand in front of them and hope he can slip strikes and land enough from range to earn a decision. Bonfim is not a dangerous striker, so I’m not worried about Thompson getting KO’d for the second time in two fights. Bonfim’s submission threat is what I’m worried about, though. Bonfim’s submissions come from all angles and at a scary pace. I don’t think Thompson will be able to fight those off for long enough to stay in the fight and will probably end up tapping from a choke. Thompson has never had elite takedown defense. With age, his 63 percent takedown defense will feel closer to 50 percent. Bonfim lands almost four takedowns per 15 minutes. He’s going to get Thompson down. Bonfim by submission is only +125. I feel strongly that this is what’s going to happen. But those odds are a little stingy. Unfortunately, the Bonfim -3.5 is even stingier at -205. For my best bet I’m going deep into DraftKings props and I’m looking at Bonfim to win in rounds one or two. I really struggle to see Thompson make it to the final bell and this at least covers me if Thompson is shot to the point that Bonfim can get him out of there with ground-and-pound. Best bet: Gabriel Bonfim to win in rounds 1-2 (+120) Calvin Kattar (+102) vs. Steve Garcia (-122) The Featherweight division have a right to be scared of Garcia. He’s one a five-fight finish streak right now, including stoppages over Melquizael Costa (see it here) and Chase Hooper (see it here). Hooper and Costa have looked pretty good since then, so that tells us what kind of level Costa has been operating at lately. Kattar, on the other hand, will lock up a rare five-fight losing streak in UFC if he gets stopped by Garcia. Last time out he was well beaten by Youssef Zalal (who won despite staying in cruise control). Before that, he was beaten by Aljamain Sterling, Arnold Allen (due to an injury) and Josh Emmett (split decision). Kattar’s toughness is the stuff of legend, thanks to the unholy beating he once took from Max Holloway. Kattar has never been stopped in his career (other than that knee injury). At 37, though, with all these wars in his past, is this the time we see that chin fade? I think so. Garcia’s punches land like a sock full of pennies. And I fear he’s going to land something really hard on Kattar. I think we’re going to see a technical knockout from Garcia, probably from ground-and-pound. I’ll take the point spread here on Garcia, believing that if Kattar doesn’t go down, Garcia will still take a dominant decision (also because Garcia by KO was only +165). Best bet: Steve Garcia -3.5 (+110) Nate Landwehr (+220) vs. Morgan Charriere (-270) Landwehr got styled on in his last fight. Doo Ho Choi looked incredible as he out-struck and out-wrestled and eventually finished “The Train” (see it here). Before that, Landwehr scored a comeback technical knockout on Jamall Emmers (see it here). In his early UFC career, Landwehr managed to get wins over Darren Elkins, L’udovit Klein and David Onama. Charriere, meanwhile, is coming off a unanimous decision loss to Nathaniel Wood where he looked good, not great. Before that, he blew away Gabriel Miranda with a left hook (see it here). Landwehr is a hard-nosed brawler who is willing to eat two shot to land one. He’s a bit like Elkins without the grappling (as exposed by how often Choi took and held him down). I think this is a very tough match-up for him, against Charriere who has looked good against opponents who charge at him. Both these guys absorb more significant strikes than they land (which is a big red flag for me), but Charriere’s negative differential is higher. Charriere is also giving up three inches in the reach department. Even so, I think Charriere’s counter punching will be the story of this fight. Landwehr doesn’t exactly fight behind his jab and pick his shots. He’ll be crashing forward trying to overwhelm Charriere. In this situation, I like Charriere to respond with something hard that puts Landwehr down. Charriere reminds me of a striker in football/soccer who misses the goal when he’s given too much time to think about his shot, but who can score on instinct when the ball comes to him and he has to react without thinking. That’s how I see Charriere getting his finish here. Best bet: Morgan Charriere moneyline (-220) Vitor Petrino (-700) vs. Austen Lane (+500) Petrino’s shiny 11-0 record was dulled by Anthony Smith and Dustin Jacoby last year. Smith scored a quick guillotine on the Brazilian (see it here) in Brazil. Then Jacoby scored a late knockout in a very boring fight (see it here). Lane, meanwhile, was KO’d by Mario Pinto last time out (see it here). Before that, he successfully fraud checked Robelis Despaigne. Prior to that fight, he was starched by Jhonata Diniz (see it here). If it wasn’t for Tuco Tokkos, Lane might be the worst fighter on a UFC main card this year. Lane has a terrible 40 percent defense on significant strikes. That’s a death sentence at Heavyweight. For the most part in his career, big shots have been able to find Lane and he’s been stopped more than your average bear (all six of his defeats are by knockout). He’s been stopped so much, that you wonder whether the 37 year old should still get a license. But, this is MMA, right? We’ll let anyone fight. Petrino came to UFC with a reputation for vicious striking, but we’ve not seen much of that in the Octagon. What we have seen has been pretty slow and telegraphed. Is that still too fast and unpredictable for Lane, though? Lane has a decent-size advantage against Petrino and I can actually see him taking Petrino down and laying on him for a round or two. However, whenever they are standing I’m worried that Lane is one punch away from being laid out. This is what we saw in the Diniz fight. Since they start rounds standing, I have to give this to Petrino. I’m not very enthusiastic about the pick, though. The round total is 1.5. I’ll go with the over, thinking Lane will get his early takedown and Petrino will continue to underwhelm, even in a winning effort. Best bet: Over 1.5 rounds (+135) Junior Tafa (-166) vs. Tuco Tokkos (+140) Tafa put away super short notice opponent Sean Sharaf back in Oct. 2024. That was his first fight since being heel hooked by Valter Walker (who fights further down the card). Before that, Tafa was TKO’d by Marcos Rogerio de Lima (see it here). Tokkos, meanwhile, stifled Navajo Stirling last time out, losing just by decision to the super hyped prospect. Before that he was submitted by Oumar Sy, with Sy locking up the rear-naked choke when Tokkos was mugging for the commentary booth. Tokkos, as referenced earlier, is probably the worst main card fighter of the year. He’s not shown us much of anything thus far in his UFC career. He did well to hang in there against Stirling, but he offered very little offensive threat. Stirling’s passivity was mostly to blame for that awful fight going the distance. Tafa isn’t much better. He’s 2-3 in UFC and the two guys he beat are well below UFC quality. I think Tafa wins this, thanks to how hittable Tokkos is (4.99 significant strikes absorbed per minute and just 33 percent significant strike defense). I wouldn’t be surprised if we get another stinker, though, that goes the distance with a decision that could go to either guy. Because I’m not sold on Tafa, over 1.5 rounds looks quite appealing. Best bet: Over 1.5 rounds (+105) UFC Nashville ‘Prelims’ Under Card Odds Max Griffin (+250) vs. Chris Curtis (-310) This is our featured “Prelim”? I guess this slot really is just, “the fight before the main card” now. The 39-year-old Griffin was tapped by Michael Chiesa in Dec. 2024. He’s been win-loss-win-loss for the past few years, with the wins being split decisions over Jeremiah Wells and Tim Means. The 37-year-old Curtis is coming off trying to separate Sean Strickland from some dude in a regional MMA cage. In his last UFC fight, Curtis lost a controversial fight with Roman Kopylov (see it here). That fight was officially ruled a head kick knockout loss at 4:59 of round three. Many felt the fight could have been left for the remaining second and then have the judges decide (I scored it for Kopylov anyways). Griffin is an okay striker and wrestler, but at 39, his potency in either area needs to be questioned. Curtis, who isn’t much younger, seems to still be a reliable and creative volume striker. His very good takedown defense probably holds up to the level needed to stay up against Griffin, too. I think there’s a chance Curtis gets a stoppage in this fight, but it might come late. I’m not going to mess around with any round betting here and instead just go with Curtis on the moneyline. Best bet: Chris Curtis moneyline (-310) Jake Matthews (+124) vs. Chidi Njokuani (-148) Both these guys are on good runs and coming off decisive wins. It’s a little surprising to see them matched up here on the “Prelims.” Matthews beat Francisco Prado by unanimous decision in February. Last year, he defeated Phil Rowe. Prior to that, he managed to make it to a losing decision against the undefeated Michael Morales. Njokuani, meanwhile, lit up Elizeu Zaleski dos Santos on the co-main of an APEX card in March (see it here). He did miss weight for that one, though. Prior to that TKO he beat Jared Gooden and Rhys McKee. Njokuani is very big for the weight class. He’s four inches taller than Matthews and will have a long seven-inch reach advantage. That reach could be significant, as it was in Njokuani’s destruction of Dos Santos. Njokuani’s reach gets even more deadlier when you consider he has the best accuracy rate for sig. strikes in the division at 62 percent. The only reason he isn’t the official leader in that stat at Welterweight is because his last two fights have technically been Catchweights (due to his weigh-in misses). The 62 percent is better than Gunnar Nelson’s official best mark of 60.6 percent and all the other killers in this rejuvenated weight class. Matthews is no slouch, though. He’s an intelligent and well rounded fighter. He probably knows he can’t win a kickboxing match and I think he’s going to try and make this an ugly brawl against the fence. He’ll look to grind on Njokuani and land a few takedowns. That might be tough, though, given Njokuani’s 75 percent takedown defense. Ultimately, I think Njokuani is going to prevent himself getting taken down in this fight. And, if Matthews, won’t let him strike from range, I still think Njokuani has a good shot at landing heavy strikes right inside Matthews’ kitchen. Njokuani’s Muay Thai style is perfect for clinch fighting, so he might find a home for some good elbows and knees. The round total for this one is set at 1.5 for some reason. The over on that is -298, so no value there. And I don’t think there’s a finish in this fight. I’ll just go with the Njokuani moneyline. Best bet: Chidi Njokuani moneyline (-148) Lauren Murphy (+440) vs. Eduarda Moura (-600) Murphy has been out of action since her bruising loss to Jessica Andrade in Jan. 2023. Before that, she dominated the un-retired Miesha Tate. Before those fights, she was TKO’d while trying to get the belt off Valentina Shevchenko. Moura, meanwhile, took a decision over Veronica Hardy in her Flyweight debut last year. That fight came after she misses weight in back-to-back Strawweight bouts. I get that Murphy has been out awhile, and that she’s 42, but Vegas is showing a lot of faith in Moura with these lines. Despite her age and inactivity as of late, I bet Murphy still “has that dog in her” and I think she will bring a lot of pressure to Moura. Moura has managed to package together wins thanks to her takedowns. Murphy’s takedown defense has been solid over her career (69 percent). The big question is whether Murphy still has good takedown defense or not. If she keeps this fight standing I think she has a good chance to take a close decision. If she is taken down, I think Moura should be able to keep her down and get a pretty comfortable decision. Either way, I think we’re going to decision. Best bet: Over 2.5 rounds (-330) Kennedy Nzechukwu (-205) vs. Valter Walker (+170) Nzechukwu is undefeated (2-0) in UFC’s Heavyweight division. In Dec. 2024, he scored a first round technical knockout over Lukasz Brzeski (see it here). Walker, on the other hand, lost to Brzeski, by decision, in his UFC debut. Since then he’s heel hooked both Junior Tafa (who didn’t like it one bit) and Don’Tale Mayes. Nzechukwu’s striking should be too much for Walker to handle. However, Nzechukwu is a little ungainly and I can totally see him getting caught by Walker’s leg locks, perhaps even after scoring a knockdown. This match-up really seems ripe for some Heavyweight nuttiness. I think it’s best to play the under in this situation, especially with the round total set at 2.5 (I was sure it would be 1.5). Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (-105) Mitch Ramirez (+700) vs. Mike Davis (-1000) Ramirez was stopped by Thiago Moises leg kicks in his last fight (see those here). His only other Octagon appearance was a walloping from Carlos Prates on Contender Series. In the opposite corner, Davis returned from a year long lay-off to fight Fares Ziam in February. He looked out of sorts and was possibly carrying an injury in that fight. He seemed to be trying to minimize damage more so than win a fight. That unanimous decision was his first UFC loss since being submitted by Gilbert Burns in 2019. He’s won four UFC fights between those losses. If the Davis we’re used to seeing shows up, then he should win this without too much trouble (as reflected in those betting lines). I think we’ll see the good version of Davis in this fight and if that happens, then his funky grappling should lead to a convincing win, probably by stoppage. Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (-180) Fatima Kline (-1200) vs. Melissa Martinez (+750) Kline was fed to the wolves on her UFC debut, coming in on short notice and up a weight class to take on Jasmine Jasudavicius. She got dominated by the bigger fighter in that bout, but rebounded with a technical knockout over Victoria Dudakova (see it here). Prior to joining UFC, Kline was a champ in the CFFC organization. She also has BJJ black belt under Mike Wacker. Martinez, meanwhile, is 1-1 in UFC with a decision win over Alice Ardelean and a decision loss to Elise Reed. She’s a former champ in the Combate organization. Martinez — who is just 5’2” — should be fighting at Atomweight (and UFC should have an Atomweight division). Kline is going to have a lot of size and strength over her (not much reach, though). I think that size difference will be most notable on the ground and I think Kline is going to use that to get a submission. Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (+114) UFC Nashville Long Shots! text: MMA Junkie analyst Dan Tom goes in-depth to break down the biggest fights in the UFC. Today, he takes a closer look at the UFC on ESPN 70 main event between Derrick Lewis and Tallison Teixeira. Derrick Lewis UFC on ESPN 70 preview Staple info: Record: 28-12 MMA, 19-10 UFC Height: 6'3" Age: 40 Weight: 261 lbs. Reach: 79" Last fight: TKO win over Rodrigo Nascimento (May 11, 2024) Camp: Main Street Boxing and Muay Thai (Texas) Stance/striking style: Orthodox/kickboxing Risk management: Fair Supplemental info: + Legacy FC heavyweight title + Regional MMA accolades + 23 KO victories + 1 submission win + 9 first-round finishes + KO power + Dangerous overhands and uppercuts + Underrated kicks and knees + Strong inside the clinch ^ Strikes well off the breaks + Shows improved wrestling + Deceptive scrambling/getup ability + Devastating ground striker Tallison Teixeira UFC on ESPN 70 preview Staple info: Record: 8-0 MMA, 1-0 UFC Height: 6'7" Age: 25 Weight: 259 lbs. Reach: 83" Last fight: TKO win over Justin Tafa (Feb. 8, 2025) Camp: Team Lucas Mineiro (Brazil) Stance/striking style: Orthodox/kickboxing Risk management: Fair Supplemental info: + Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt + Multiple grappling accolades + Muay Thai red kruang + 7 KO victories + 1 submission win + 8 first-round finishes + KO power + Dangerous right hand + Dynamic kicks ^ Variates looks and levels + Servicable takedown game ^ Favors doubles along the fence + Competent submission skills Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira point of interest: Heavyweight hands The main event in Nashville features a heavyweight showdown between Derrick Lewis and Tallison Teixeira. Stepping onto the scene as an unabashed brawler, Lewis has shown some signs of improvement underneath the scary destructions that often take place in his fights. An athletic mover for his size, Lewis can throw accurate knees and head kicks with little signs of struggle. A downright scary distance closer when he chooses to be, Lewis can force his opponents into the fence whether or not he lands on them, almost in a juggernaut-like fashion. With a frame that is hard to control in close, the 40-year-old slugger does his best work when striking off the breaks, maintaining a dangerous potency in small spaces that go deep into the fight. Lewis also has an appetite for the counter, showing that he’s not beyond setting traps and playing possum in order to draw his opponents into his uncanny power. That said, Lewis will still need to respect what is coming his way this Saturday. Enter Teixiera. Although Teixiera is clearly lacking in the experience department, I can see why many are high on the prospects of this young heavyweight. Despite Teixeira's insane height, he actually moves quite well for a big man and is not afraid to utilize tools like a long jab. The Brazilian also packs wicked power in his rear hand, but kicks, particularly to the body, may serve Teixeira well in this spot. Teixeira may not go to the body as much as I'd like, but he has shown some decent change-ups from front teeps to Thai kicks that help exentuate his length. Teixeira will blitz forward in combination when he's feeling in stride, but he'll need to be careful about crowding his work into the clinch – an area where Lewis can stage comebacks. Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira breakdown: Potential grappling threats Considering the high potential for chaos on the feet, no one should be shocked if this party hits the floor. Despite Lewis showing improved offensive wrestling and a surprising ability to hit inside trips in recent years, Teixeira is the more dangerous grappler on paper. Although we've seen very little of Teixeira's ground game, the 25-year-old owns a Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt and has apparently been grappling since childhood. Teixeira only has one submission win on his resume, but between that win being an inverted triangle-armbar to his history training with Antonio Rodrigo Nogueira, I suspect that the lengthy heavyweight has solid dexterity to boot. When it comes to wrestling, Teixeira has shown a servicable double leg he can go to when his opponents find their back against the fence. That said, effectively taking down and grounding someone like Lewis is easier said than done. Traditionally dealing with fighters who are trying to grapple him, Lewis wields deceptively effective counter-grappling tactics. Whether he’s hoisting his opponent up with a whizzer or shucking someone off with an underhook, Lewis has been hard to take down along the fence, as single legs or outside trips in open space seem to be what gets him grounded most. Even when successfully taken down, Lewis still offers a lot of sneaky static in regard to stymying submission attempts and strikes. Like a sand shark lying in wait, Lewis plays a conservative game when put on his back, keeping his arms in tight for safety while waiting for the right moment to explode (usually timing his opposition when they’re in transition). Once allowed the smallest of space for momentum, Lewis will force his way to his base, turtling to a tripod position to stand. As someone who is a fan of this style of get-up, I can tell you that it can be a nightmare to encounter when executed properly. For example, Lewis – while keeping his base firmly beneath him – will maintain an angle on his back that resembles a steep ski slope. Although this tripod position invites back-takes to the naked eye, the downward slope Lewis keeps serves as a trap, making eager back takers ultimately slide forward and lose position (all while allowing the Texas native to stand back up). And if Lewis is able to end up on top via swimming for underhooks and shucking, then we could see a drastic shift in this matchup’s momentum given the hellfire of ground-and-pound he provides. Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira odds The oddsmakers and the public are favoring the undefeated fighter, listing Teixeira -245 and Lewis +186 via FanDuel. Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira prediction, pick Considering how high the MMA gambling world gets over youthful, undefeated products, I can't say that I'm surprised to see Teixeira installed as the betting favorite despite being relatively unproven. Should Teixeira come out and light Lewis up with some body kicks, then no one should be shocked if the Brazilian can find a finish soon after. That said, Lewis has had a penchant for both countering and coming back from effective body kicks – particularly against taller opponents. In fact, whenever facing fighters of a similar height to Teixeira, Lewis has traditionally done fairly well (going 3-0 in the UFC opposite the likes of Travis Browne, Alexander Volkov and Jack May). And if Teixeira decides to revert to his base of grappling, then he could find himself in a frying pan-to-frier situation. Despite logic saying that Lewis should be beatable on the ground, only a select few fighters (Daniel Cormier, Serghei Spivac and Jailton Almeida) have been able to truly out-grapple the American, as anyone who tries to grapple Lewis has traditionally done poorly. Should Teixeira fall into this classic trap, then he'll need to be careful not to end up underneath Lewis, which is almost a death sentence given his lethal ground striking. I ultimately suspect that it's a strike off the break that sparks things off for Lewis, likely after having to survive some scares first. The pick is Lewis by knockout in Round 2. Prediction: Lewis inside the distance Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira start time, how to watch As the main event, Lewis and Teixeira are expected to make their walks to the octagon at approximately 11:45 p.m. ET. title: UFC Nashville odds: Best betting props, parlays and picks | Lewis vs. Teixeira
text: UFC Nashville goes down this weekend (Sat., July 12, 2025) inside Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tennessee. The main event features Heavyweights with Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira. Lewis, a divisional stalwart, is hoping to get past the UFC neophyte and secure a fight with new UFC champion, Tom Aspinall. When it comes to the rest of the UFC Nashville card, there’s not too much to write home about. The co-main is Stephen Thompson vs. Gabriel Bonfim. Rounding out the main card is Calvin Kattar vs. Steve Garcia, Nate Landwehr vs. Morgan Charriere, Vitor Petrino vs. Austin Lane and Junior Tafa vs Tuco Tokkos. UFC Nashville’s “Prelims” are headlined by Max Griffin vs. Chris Curtis. The “Prelims” also have Jake Matthews vs. Chidi Njokuani and Lauren Murphy vs. Eduarda Moura. As always, there’s lots to bet on this card and we’ve got odds for all the fights below: UFC Nashville Main Card Money Line Odds Derrick Lewis (+220) vs. Tallison Teixeira (-270) The towering Teixeira is just 8-0 and two fights into his UFC career. He debuted in the Octagon with a Contender Series first round knockout over Arthur Lopes. In his proper debut, he put away Justin Tafa in 35 seconds (see it here). Lewis — who turned 40 this year — is coming off a third round technical knockout win over Rodrigo Nascimento. Before that, he lost a five-round decision to Jailton Almeida. And before that, he scored a 33-second win over Marcos Rogerio Lima (see it here). That win snapped a three fight losing skid (all finishes) where he lost to Serghei Spivac, Sergei Pavlovich and Tai Tuivasa. There’s not much to scout when it comes to Teixeira. He’s very tall and very long and he’s coming into UFC in his athletic prime at only 25 years-old. Lewis is giving up four inches of height and four inches of reach to the young Brazilian. The last time Lewis fought someone with that kind of reach it was Pavlovich and he lasted just 55 seconds. Lewis is capable of the spectacular and shocking in an Octagon. But, it really feels like the odds are stacked against him here, with a fighter so long, so powerful and with so much youth on his side. Lewis’ defense against significant strikes is just 40 percent. That spells a lot of trouble for “The Black Beast” against a man who, so far, has landed 14.61 significant strikes per-minute across his three Octagon appearances. In Heavyweight, it only takes one punch to win, a lot of the times, but I have to favor the man who is going to be landing dozens of them in a round (if it makes it that far). The round total for this fight is set at 1.5. I think the under is most likely, as do many others. The odds are just -210 for that prop. Teixeira by KO/TKO/DQ is a laughable -185. And Teixeira to win by strikes in round one is just -125. Clearly, there’s not much value if you believe Teixeira is going to quickly separate Lewis from his consciousness (as I do). For my best bet, I’m going to go for a winning round and method of victory parlay. I’m taking round one and TKO/KO/DQ. This covers me just in case Lewis does something silly/outstanding in the first round in Nashville. Best bet: Fight to end in Round 1 by KO/TKO/DQ (-150) Stephen Thompson (+320) vs. Gabriel Bonfim (-410) Thompson is coming off a third round knockout loss to Joaquin Buckley (see it here). Before that, he was submitted by Shavkat Rakhmonov (see it here). His last win was over Kevin Holland, when Holland retired at the end of round four. Bonfim, on the other hand, choked out Khaos Williams in his last fight (see it here). Before that, he took a decision over Ange Loosa. Before those fights he lost, as a big favorite, to Nicolas Dalby via technical knockout (see it here). I don’t think Thompson is long for this sport. He turned 42 this year and his fighting style isn’t great for masking your age. He can’t hide behind takedowns and take dangerous finishers out of their comfort zones. He has to stand in front of them and hope he can slip strikes and land enough from range to earn a decision. Bonfim is not a dangerous striker, so I’m not worried about Thompson getting KO’d for the second time in two fights. Bonfim’s submission threat is what I’m worried about, though. Bonfim’s submissions come from all angles and at a scary pace. I don’t think Thompson will be able to fight those off for long enough to stay in the fight and will probably end up tapping from a choke. Thompson has never had elite takedown defense. With age, his 63 percent takedown defense will feel closer to 50 percent. Bonfim lands almost four takedowns per 15 minutes. He’s going to get Thompson down. Bonfim by submission is only +125. I feel strongly that this is what’s going to happen. But those odds are a little stingy. Unfortunately, the Bonfim -3.5 is even stingier at -205. For my best bet I’m going deep into DraftKings props and I’m looking at Bonfim to win in rounds one or two. I really struggle to see Thompson make it to the final bell and this at least covers me if Thompson is shot to the point that Bonfim can get him out of there with ground-and-pound. Best bet: Gabriel Bonfim to win in rounds 1-2 (+120) Calvin Kattar (+102) vs. Steve Garcia (-122) The Featherweight division have a right to be scared of Garcia. He’s one a five-fight finish streak right now, including stoppages over Melquizael Costa (see it here) and Chase Hooper (see it here). Hooper and Costa have looked pretty good since then, so that tells us what kind of level Costa has been operating at lately. Kattar, on the other hand, will lock up a rare five-fight losing streak in UFC if he gets stopped by Garcia. Last time out he was well beaten by Youssef Zalal (who won despite staying in cruise control). Before that, he was beaten by Aljamain Sterling, Arnold Allen (due to an injury) and Josh Emmett (split decision). Kattar’s toughness is the stuff of legend, thanks to the unholy beating he once took from Max Holloway. Kattar has never been stopped in his career (other than that knee injury). At 37, though, with all these wars in his past, is this the time we see that chin fade? I think so. Garcia’s punches land like a sock full of pennies. And I fear he’s going to land something really hard on Kattar. I think we’re going to see a technical knockout from Garcia, probably from ground-and-pound. I’ll take the point spread here on Garcia, believing that if Kattar doesn’t go down, Garcia will still take a dominant decision (also because Garcia by KO was only +165). Best bet: Steve Garcia -3.5 (+110) Nate Landwehr (+220) vs. Morgan Charriere (-270) Landwehr got styled on in his last fight. Doo Ho Choi looked incredible as he out-struck and out-wrestled and eventually finished “The Train” (see it here). Before that, Landwehr scored a comeback technical knockout on Jamall Emmers (see it here). In his early UFC career, Landwehr managed to get wins over Darren Elkins, L’udovit Klein and David Onama. Charriere, meanwhile, is coming off a unanimous decision loss to Nathaniel Wood where he looked good, not great. Before that, he blew away Gabriel Miranda with a left hook (see it here). Landwehr is a hard-nosed brawler who is willing to eat two shot to land one. He’s a bit like Elkins without the grappling (as exposed by how often Choi took and held him down). I think this is a very tough match-up for him, against Charriere who has looked good against opponents who charge at him. Both these guys absorb more significant strikes than they land (which is a big red flag for me), but Charriere’s negative differential is higher. Charriere is also giving up three inches in the reach department. Even so, I think Charriere’s counter punching will be the story of this fight. Landwehr doesn’t exactly fight behind his jab and pick his shots. He’ll be crashing forward trying to overwhelm Charriere. In this situation, I like Charriere to respond with something hard that puts Landwehr down. Charriere reminds me of a striker in football/soccer who misses the goal when he’s given too much time to think about his shot, but who can score on instinct when the ball comes to him and he has to react without thinking. That’s how I see Charriere getting his finish here. Best bet: Morgan Charriere moneyline (-220) Vitor Petrino (-700) vs. Austen Lane (+500) Petrino’s shiny 11-0 record was dulled by Anthony Smith and Dustin Jacoby last year. Smith scored a quick guillotine on the Brazilian (see it here) in Brazil. Then Jacoby scored a late knockout in a very boring fight (see it here). Lane, meanwhile, was KO’d by Mario Pinto last time out (see it here). Before that, he successfully fraud checked Robelis Despaigne. Prior to that fight, he was starched by Jhonata Diniz (see it here). If it wasn’t for Tuco Tokkos, Lane might be the worst fighter on a UFC main card this year. Lane has a terrible 40 percent defense on significant strikes. That’s a death sentence at Heavyweight. For the most part in his career, big shots have been able to find Lane and he’s been stopped more than your average bear (all six of his defeats are by knockout). He’s been stopped so much, that you wonder whether the 37 year old should still get a license. But, this is MMA, right? We’ll let anyone fight. Petrino came to UFC with a reputation for vicious striking, but we’ve not seen much of that in the Octagon. What we have seen has been pretty slow and telegraphed. Is that still too fast and unpredictable for Lane, though? Lane has a decent-size advantage against Petrino and I can actually see him taking Petrino down and laying on him for a round or two. However, whenever they are standing I’m worried that Lane is one punch away from being laid out. This is what we saw in the Diniz fight. Since they start rounds standing, I have to give this to Petrino. I’m not very enthusiastic about the pick, though. The round total is 1.5. I’ll go with the over, thinking Lane will get his early takedown and Petrino will continue to underwhelm, even in a winning effort. Best bet: Over 1.5 rounds (+135) Junior Tafa (-166) vs. Tuco Tokkos (+140) Tafa put away super short notice opponent Sean Sharaf back in Oct. 2024. That was his first fight since being heel hooked by Valter Walker (who fights further down the card). Before that, Tafa was TKO’d by Marcos Rogerio de Lima (see it here). Tokkos, meanwhile, stifled Navajo Stirling last time out, losing just by decision to the super hyped prospect. Before that he was submitted by Oumar Sy, with Sy locking up the rear-naked choke when Tokkos was mugging for the commentary booth. Tokkos, as referenced earlier, is probably the worst main card fighter of the year. He’s not shown us much of anything thus far in his UFC career. He did well to hang in there against Stirling, but he offered very little offensive threat. Stirling’s passivity was mostly to blame for that awful fight going the distance. Tafa isn’t much better. He’s 2-3 in UFC and the two guys he beat are well below UFC quality. I think Tafa wins this, thanks to how hittable Tokkos is (4.99 significant strikes absorbed per minute and just 33 percent significant strike defense). I wouldn’t be surprised if we get another stinker, though, that goes the distance with a decision that could go to either guy. Because I’m not sold on Tafa, over 1.5 rounds looks quite appealing. Best bet: Over 1.5 rounds (+105) UFC Nashville ‘Prelims’ Under Card Odds Max Griffin (+250) vs. Chris Curtis (-310) This is our featured “Prelim”? I guess this slot really is just, “the fight before the main card” now. The 39-year-old Griffin was tapped by Michael Chiesa in Dec. 2024. He’s been win-loss-win-loss for the past few years, with the wins being split decisions over Jeremiah Wells and Tim Means. The 37-year-old Curtis is coming off trying to separate Sean Strickland from some dude in a regional MMA cage. In his last UFC fight, Curtis lost a controversial fight with Roman Kopylov (see it here). That fight was officially ruled a head kick knockout loss at 4:59 of round three. Many felt the fight could have been left for the remaining second and then have the judges decide (I scored it for Kopylov anyways). Griffin is an okay striker and wrestler, but at 39, his potency in either area needs to be questioned. Curtis, who isn’t much younger, seems to still be a reliable and creative volume striker. His very good takedown defense probably holds up to the level needed to stay up against Griffin, too. I think there’s a chance Curtis gets a stoppage in this fight, but it might come late. I’m not going to mess around with any round betting here and instead just go with Curtis on the moneyline. Best bet: Chris Curtis moneyline (-310) Jake Matthews (+124) vs. Chidi Njokuani (-148) Both these guys are on good runs and coming off decisive wins. It’s a little surprising to see them matched up here on the “Prelims.” Matthews beat Francisco Prado by unanimous decision in February. Last year, he defeated Phil Rowe. Prior to that, he managed to make it to a losing decision against the undefeated Michael Morales. Njokuani, meanwhile, lit up Elizeu Zaleski dos Santos on the co-main of an APEX card in March (see it here). He did miss weight for that one, though. Prior to that TKO he beat Jared Gooden and Rhys McKee. Njokuani is very big for the weight class. He’s four inches taller than Matthews and will have a long seven-inch reach advantage. That reach could be significant, as it was in Njokuani’s destruction of Dos Santos. Njokuani’s reach gets even more deadlier when you consider he has the best accuracy rate for sig. strikes in the division at 62 percent. The only reason he isn’t the official leader in that stat at Welterweight is because his last two fights have technically been Catchweights (due to his weigh-in misses). The 62 percent is better than Gunnar Nelson’s official best mark of 60.6 percent and all the other killers in this rejuvenated weight class. Matthews is no slouch, though. He’s an intelligent and well rounded fighter. He probably knows he can’t win a kickboxing match and I think he’s going to try and make this an ugly brawl against the fence. He’ll look to grind on Njokuani and land a few takedowns. That might be tough, though, given Njokuani’s 75 percent takedown defense. Ultimately, I think Njokuani is going to prevent himself getting taken down in this fight. And, if Matthews, won’t let him strike from range, I still think Njokuani has a good shot at landing heavy strikes right inside Matthews’ kitchen. Njokuani’s Muay Thai style is perfect for clinch fighting, so he might find a home for some good elbows and knees. The round total for this one is set at 1.5 for some reason. The over on that is -298, so no value there. And I don’t think there’s a finish in this fight. I’ll just go with the Njokuani moneyline. Best bet: Chidi Njokuani moneyline (-148) Lauren Murphy (+440) vs. Eduarda Moura (-600) Murphy has been out of action since her bruising loss to Jessica Andrade in Jan. 2023. Before that, she dominated the un-retired Miesha Tate. Before those fights, she was TKO’d while trying to get the belt off Valentina Shevchenko. Moura, meanwhile, took a decision over Veronica Hardy in her Flyweight debut last year. That fight came after she misses weight in back-to-back Strawweight bouts. I get that Murphy has been out awhile, and that she’s 42, but Vegas is showing a lot of faith in Moura with these lines. Despite her age and inactivity as of late, I bet Murphy still “has that dog in her” and I think she will bring a lot of pressure to Moura. Moura has managed to package together wins thanks to her takedowns. Murphy’s takedown defense has been solid over her career (69 percent). The big question is whether Murphy still has good takedown defense or not. If she keeps this fight standing I think she has a good chance to take a close decision. If she is taken down, I think Moura should be able to keep her down and get a pretty comfortable decision. Either way, I think we’re going to decision. Best bet: Over 2.5 rounds (-330) Kennedy Nzechukwu (-205) vs. Valter Walker (+170) Nzechukwu is undefeated (2-0) in UFC’s Heavyweight division. In Dec. 2024, he scored a first round technical knockout over Lukasz Brzeski (see it here). Walker, on the other hand, lost to Brzeski, by decision, in his UFC debut. Since then he’s heel hooked both Junior Tafa (who didn’t like it one bit) and Don’Tale Mayes. Nzechukwu’s striking should be too much for Walker to handle. However, Nzechukwu is a little ungainly and I can totally see him getting caught by Walker’s leg locks, perhaps even after scoring a knockdown. This match-up really seems ripe for some Heavyweight nuttiness. I think it’s best to play the under in this situation, especially with the round total set at 2.5 (I was sure it would be 1.5). Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (-105) Mitch Ramirez (+700) vs. Mike Davis (-1000) Ramirez was stopped by Thiago Moises leg kicks in his last fight (see those here). His only other Octagon appearance was a walloping from Carlos Prates on Contender Series. In the opposite corner, Davis returned from a year long lay-off to fight Fares Ziam in February. He looked out of sorts and was possibly carrying an injury in that fight. He seemed to be trying to minimize damage more so than win a fight. That unanimous decision was his first UFC loss since being submitted by Gilbert Burns in 2019. He’s won four UFC fights between those losses. If the Davis we’re used to seeing shows up, then he should win this without too much trouble (as reflected in those betting lines). I think we’ll see the good version of Davis in this fight and if that happens, then his funky grappling should lead to a convincing win, probably by stoppage. Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (-180) Fatima Kline (-1200) vs. Melissa Martinez (+750) Kline was fed to the wolves on her UFC debut, coming in on short notice and up a weight class to take on Jasmine Jasudavicius. She got dominated by the bigger fighter in that bout, but rebounded with a technical knockout over Victoria Dudakova (see it here). Prior to joining UFC, Kline was a champ in the CFFC organization. She also has BJJ black belt under Mike Wacker. Martinez, meanwhile, is 1-1 in UFC with a decision win over Alice Ardelean and a decision loss to Elise Reed. She’s a former champ in the Combate organization. Martinez — who is just 5’2” — should be fighting at Atomweight (and UFC should have an Atomweight division). Kline is going to have a lot of size and strength over her (not much reach, though). I think that size difference will be most notable on the ground and I think Kline is going to use that to get a submission. Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (+114) UFC Nashville Long Shots! Here’s a couple of long shots for Saturday night’s action. Derrick Lewis to Win and Over 3.5 (+1000) Let’s just imagine that Teixeira is being over-hyped and that his best work has all come against tomato cans. And let’s imagine that Lewis is going to rewind the clock and survive a lot of early punishment. Maybe Teixeira punches himself out? And then, maybe Lewis uncorks one of his classic right hooks that knocks him out cold? It’s not impossible, right? It’s Heavyweight after all. Three-fight parlay: Tallison Teixeira, Steve Garcia, Valter Walker (+568) Despite that first long shot bet, I’m reasonably confident that Teixeira is legit enough to be better than a 40-year-old Lewis. I’m also pretty confident that Steve Garcia will add to his impressive winning streak when he meets Kattar. Walker is my wild card in this parlay and he’s here to add some value. Nzechukwu has looked good at Heavyweight so far, but he’s not faced anyone like Walker. Morgan Charriere to win by KO/TKO/DQ and over 1.5 rounds (+550) I used DraftKings to make my own same game parlay here. It kind of kills me to do it, since I really like Landwehr. Unfortunately, I just think he will fight right into Charriere’s strengths and walk into something nasty. title: Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira prediction, pick: Who gets KO'd at UFC Nashville?
text: MMA Junkie analyst Dan Tom goes in-depth to break down the biggest fights in the UFC. Today, he takes a closer look at the UFC on ESPN 70 main event between Derrick Lewis and Tallison Teixeira. Derrick Lewis UFC on ESPN 70 preview Staple info: Record: 28-12 MMA, 19-10 UFC Height: 6'3" Age: 40 Weight: 261 lbs. Reach: 79" Last fight: TKO win over Rodrigo Nascimento (May 11, 2024) Camp: Main Street Boxing and Muay Thai (Texas) Stance/striking style: Orthodox/kickboxing Risk management: Fair Supplemental info: + Legacy FC heavyweight title + Regional MMA accolades + 23 KO victories + 1 submission win + 9 first-round finishes + KO power + Dangerous overhands and uppercuts + Underrated kicks and knees + Strong inside the clinch ^ Strikes well off the breaks + Shows improved wrestling + Deceptive scrambling/getup ability + Devastating ground striker Tallison Teixeira UFC on ESPN 70 preview Staple info: Record: 8-0 MMA, 1-0 UFC Height: 6'7" Age: 25 Weight: 259 lbs. Reach: 83" Last fight: TKO win over Justin Tafa (Feb. 8, 2025) Camp: Team Lucas Mineiro (Brazil) Stance/striking style: Orthodox/kickboxing Risk management: Fair Supplemental info: + Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt + Multiple grappling accolades + Muay Thai red kruang + 7 KO victories + 1 submission win + 8 first-round finishes + KO power + Dangerous right hand + Dynamic kicks ^ Variates looks and levels + Servicable takedown game ^ Favors doubles along the fence + Competent submission skills Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira point of interest: Heavyweight hands The main event in Nashville features a heavyweight showdown between Derrick Lewis and Tallison Teixeira. Stepping onto the scene as an unabashed brawler, Lewis has shown some signs of improvement underneath the scary destructions that often take place in his fights. An athletic mover for his size, Lewis can throw accurate knees and head kicks with little signs of struggle. A downright scary distance closer when he chooses to be, Lewis can force his opponents into the fence whether or not he lands on them, almost in a juggernaut-like fashion. With a frame that is hard to control in close, the 40-year-old slugger does his best work when striking off the breaks, maintaining a dangerous potency in small spaces that go deep into the fight. Lewis also has an appetite for the counter, showing that he’s not beyond setting traps and playing possum in order to draw his opponents into his uncanny power. That said, Lewis will still need to respect what is coming his way this Saturday. Enter Teixiera. Although Teixiera is clearly lacking in the experience department, I can see why many are high on the prospects of this young heavyweight. Despite Teixeira's insane height, he actually moves quite well for a big man and is not afraid to utilize tools like a long jab. The Brazilian also packs wicked power in his rear hand, but kicks, particularly to the body, may serve Teixeira well in this spot. Teixeira may not go to the body as much as I'd like, but he has shown some decent change-ups from front teeps to Thai kicks that help exentuate his length. Teixeira will blitz forward in combination when he's feeling in stride, but he'll need to be careful about crowding his work into the clinch – an area where Lewis can stage comebacks. Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira breakdown: Potential grappling threats Considering the high potential for chaos on the feet, no one should be shocked if this party hits the floor. Despite Lewis showing improved offensive wrestling and a surprising ability to hit inside trips in recent years, Teixeira is the more dangerous grappler on paper. Although we've seen very little of Teixeira's ground game, the 25-year-old owns a Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt and has apparently been grappling since childhood. Teixeira only has one submission win on his resume, but between that win being an inverted triangle-armbar to his history training with Antonio Rodrigo Nogueira, I suspect that the lengthy heavyweight has solid dexterity to boot. When it comes to wrestling, Teixeira has shown a servicable double leg he can go to when his opponents find their back against the fence. That said, effectively taking down and grounding someone like Lewis is easier said than done. Traditionally dealing with fighters who are trying to grapple him, Lewis wields deceptively effective counter-grappling tactics. Whether he’s hoisting his opponent up with a whizzer or shucking someone off with an underhook, Lewis has been hard to take down along the fence, as single legs or outside trips in open space seem to be what gets him grounded most. Even when successfully taken down, Lewis still offers a lot of sneaky static in regard to stymying submission attempts and strikes. Like a sand shark lying in wait, Lewis plays a conservative game when put on his back, keeping his arms in tight for safety while waiting for the right moment to explode (usually timing his opposition when they’re in transition). Once allowed the smallest of space for momentum, Lewis will force his way to his base, turtling to a tripod position to stand. As someone who is a fan of this style of get-up, I can tell you that it can be a nightmare to encounter when executed properly. For example, Lewis – while keeping his base firmly beneath him – will maintain an angle on his back that resembles a steep ski slope. Although this tripod position invites back-takes to the naked eye, the downward slope Lewis keeps serves as a trap, making eager back takers ultimately slide forward and lose position (all while allowing the Texas native to stand back up). And if Lewis is able to end up on top via swimming for underhooks and shucking, then we could see a drastic shift in this matchup’s momentum given the hellfire of ground-and-pound he provides. Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira odds The oddsmakers and the public are favoring the undefeated fighter, listing Teixeira -245 and Lewis +186 via FanDuel. Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira prediction, pick Considering how high the MMA gambling world gets over youthful, undefeated products, I can't say that I'm surprised to see Teixeira installed as the betting favorite despite being relatively unproven. Should Teixeira come out and light Lewis up with some body kicks, then no one should be shocked if the Brazilian can find a finish soon after. That said, Lewis has had a penchant for both countering and coming back from effective body kicks – particularly against taller opponents. In fact, whenever facing fighters of a similar height to Teixeira, Lewis has traditionally done fairly well (going 3-0 in the UFC opposite the likes of Travis Browne, Alexander Volkov and Jack May). And if Teixeira decides to revert to his base of grappling, then he could find himself in a frying pan-to-frier situation. Despite logic saying that Lewis should be beatable on the ground, only a select few fighters (Daniel Cormier, Serghei Spivac and Jailton Almeida) have been able to truly out-grapple the American, as anyone who tries to grapple Lewis has traditionally done poorly. Should Teixeira fall into this classic trap, then he'll need to be careful not to end up underneath Lewis, which is almost a death sentence given his lethal ground striking. I ultimately suspect that it's a strike off the break that sparks things off for Lewis, likely after having to survive some scares first. The pick is Lewis by knockout in Round 2. Prediction: Lewis inside the distance Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira start time, how to watch As the main event, Lewis and Teixeira are expected to make their walks to the octagon at approximately 11:45 p.m. ET. The fight airs on ESPN and streams on ESPN+. This article originally appeared on MMA Junkie: Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira pick, odds, time: UFC Nashville
